hero.headline: Trump delays Ukraine drone deal despite Zelensky requests
hero.teaser: The Trump administration has not signed a major drone agreement with Ukraine despite months of negotiations and direct appeals from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky.
hero.body:
The Trump administration has not yet finalized a major drone agreement with Ukraine, a delay that concerns military experts monitoring U.S. efforts to modernize its drone capabilities. Negotiations between the two countries have been underway since at least September, with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky repeatedly calling for Washington to complete the deal.

Zelensky outlined the issue during an appearance on CBS Face the Nation, explaining that Ukraine had already accommodated American testing preferences. "The US wanted to test all types of our drones. We agreed to the way they wanted to test, train with, and use our systems in the air, on land, and at sea. But we still don't have a bilateral drone deal," he said.

The Ukrainian president emphasized the potential benefits of cooperation, noting that American companies possess advanced artificial intelligence technologies that Ukraine lacks. "In turn, we have many things they don't have, due to our extensive experience on the battlefield. I think this cooperation can be huge," Zelensky stated, while acknowledging that the agreement requires Trump's approval to move forward.

Trump has been dismissive of Ukraine's drone expertise, claiming the United States does not need Ukrainian assistance in this area. However, this position contradicts developments in the Middle East, where multiple countries are actively pursuing deals to acquire Ukrainian defensive drones and training for their personnel. These nations have faced repeated Iranian attacks using the same Shahed drones that Russia deploys against Ukraine.

Zelensky noted that Ukraine has already secured drone agreements with countries in the Middle East and Europe. "Now we are preparing a big drone deal with the EU. I hope we will reach the same agreement with our American partners," he said.

The delay comes as Ukraine continues to demonstrate its drone capabilities in combat. On Sunday, Ukrainian forces struck multiple Russian energy infrastructure targets, including the Saratov oil refinery in southwestern Russia and the Lazarevo pumping station in the Kirov region northeast of Moscow, located more than 1,200 kilometers from Ukrainian-controlled territory. Ukrainian forces also attacked a fuel depot in the Rostov region.

Russia responded with its own drone strikes across Ukraine, targeting civilian areas and energy facilities. One person died in Chernihiv after a Russian drone hit a parking lot, while attacks on the city left 40,000 people without power. Russian drones also struck Dnipro and an oil refinery in the Rivne region.

Meanwhile, Zelensky announced that Ukraine had received a new Iris-T missile launcher from Germany and appealed to allies for additional air defense ammunition. He emphasized the need for more missiles to strengthen Ukraine's ability to counter Russian aerial attacks.

cards.headline: Chinese President Xi Jinping visits North Korea as Kim rejects denuclearization
cards.teaser: Xi Jinping traveled to North Korea as the regime declared its nuclear program irreversible and rejected US denuclearization efforts.
cards.body:
Chinese President Xi Jinping traveled to North Korea for a state visit, his first since 2019. The timing coincided with North Korea's unveiling of a new nuclear fuel production facility.

During the visit, Kim Jong Un's sister issued a statement rejecting denuclearization efforts, calling them an anachronistic dream. The meeting underscores the strategic partnership between Beijing and Pyongyang, with China serving as North Korea's primary diplomatic and economic partner.

cards.headline: China escalates naval patrols near Taiwan following Japan-Philippines talks
cards.teaser: China deployed coast guard vessels and its largest patrol ship east of Taiwan in response to recent discussions between Tokyo and Manila.
cards.body:
Chinese coast guard ships and research vessels conducted operations near key islands in the South China Sea and waters east of Taiwan. Beijing deployed its largest patrol ship to the region following security talks between Japan and the Philippines.

Taiwan responded by deploying its own vessels to monitor the Chinese activity. The patrols represent an escalation in Chinese military and coast guard presence around Taiwan. China views the growing security cooperation between Japan and the Philippines as a threat to its regional interests and has used naval operations to signal its opposition to such partnerships.

cards.headline: Oil Prices Spike as Industry Watches for Demand Destruction
cards.body:
Oil prices have spiked, prompting industry observers to discuss the possibility of demand destruction, a term describing a sustained drop in demand for a commodity caused by high prices. The concept, which has been used in energy markets for decades, signals a shift in consumption patterns when prices reach levels that force consumers and businesses to reduce their usage or seek alternatives.

Recent price increases have been driven by geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. A US-Iran ceasefire initially sent crude oil prices down, but renewed military escalation between Israel and Lebanon has cast doubt on whether supplies will resume flowing normally. Market uncertainty over the potential closure of the Strait of Hormuz, a critical shipping route, has pushed prices back up as traders worry about future supply constraints.

The impact on fuel costs has been immediate and severe. In Australia, diesel prices have climbed to record highs of nearly 330 cents per litre in some areas, with prices rising as much as 20 cents per litre in just two days. Petrol prices have also faced upward pressure, though they fell slightly in some capitals this week. These wholesale price increases have outpaced government fuel tax relief measures.

The Australian government has taken action to address supply concerns by helping domestic refineries bid for oil shipments on the open market. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese is traveling to Singapore to lock in ongoing fuel supplies from Australia's largest source of refined fuels. Energy Minister Chris Bowen confirmed that contracted shipments remain secure until at least mid-May and indicated that new supplies could come from multiple sources including the United States, Mexico, Singapore, Korea, and Malaysia.

Higher fuel costs create ripple effects throughout the economy. Industries dependent on petroleum products, including transportation and manufacturing, face increased operating costs that can squeeze profit margins or force price increases for consumers. Treasury officials have highlighted how the fuel crisis underscores the need for transitioning to renewable energy sources and developing more resilient supply chains.

The question now facing markets is whether current price levels will trigger demand destruction similar to previous oil shocks. When prices reached record levels in 2008, global oil consumption declined as consumers drove less and businesses reduced energy use. Whether that pattern repeats depends on several factors, including inflation rates, wage growth, energy policy decisions, and the availability of alternative fuels.

Australian officials have warned that even if the Middle East ceasefire holds and the Strait of Hormuz reopens, the effects will persist for months. Disruption to shipping transit and storage facilities in the Gulf means global supply will take considerable time to return to normal levels. Until then, consumers and businesses worldwide face uncertainty about whether they can absorb higher fuel costs or will be forced to reduce consumption.

cards.headline: 12 people shot near street festival in Toledo, Ohio
cards.body:
Gunfire erupted near a busy street festival in Toledo, Ohio on Saturday, wounding at least 12 people. Police say it appears two people fired weapons and were probably shooting at each other. The shooting sent some festival attendees scrambling for cover while others rushed to help the victims.

The victims range in age from 14 to 61 years old. Two people were critically injured in the shooting. Toledo deputy police chief Joe Heffernan described the level of violence as concerning, saying "As far as violence, this is over the top."

A search for the suspects remained ongoing as of the latest reports. No suspects were in custody. Police have not released descriptions of the individuals believed to have fired the weapons.

The shooting occurred near the Old West End Festival, an annual community event that draws large crowds to the area. The festival was taking place on a busy street when the gunfire began on Saturday. Witnesses described chaotic scenes as people tried to flee the area or take cover while others attempted to assist those who had been shot.

The wounded were transported to nearby hospitals for treatment. The ages of those injured demonstrate the indiscriminate nature of the violence, with victims spanning from early teenagers to older adults.

The incident adds to a string of public shootings at community gatherings across the United States. Toledo police are continuing their investigation and have asked anyone with information about the shooting to come forward. Authorities are working to identify the two individuals responsible for the gunfire.

The festival had drawn significant numbers of people to the Old West End neighborhood when the violence erupted. The chaotic aftermath highlighted how quickly a community gathering can turn dangerous when armed conflict breaks out in a crowded public space.

Police have focused their investigation on determining the motive behind the shooting and identifying the two suspects. The fact that the shooters appeared to be targeting each other rather than the crowd suggests the incident may have stemmed from a personal conflict, though authorities have not confirmed the underlying cause.

The shooting has renewed concerns about public safety at community events in Toledo. The festival, which is an annual tradition designed to bring neighbors together, instead became the scene of a traumatic incident affecting dozens of people who witnessed the violence or were directly harmed.

As the investigation continues, police are urging anyone with information to contact them. Investigators are likely reviewing surveillance footage from the area and gathering witness statements to help identify and locate the two suspects responsible for the shooting.

cards.headline: Gunman kills one and wounds several in central Israel shooting
cards.body:
A shooting attack in central Israel killed at least one person and wounded several others on Sunday. Israeli authorities characterized the incident as a terrorist attack.

Hamas praised the assault but did not claim responsibility for carrying it out. The Palestinian militant group's statement came as Israeli emergency services responded to the scene in central Israel.

The attack adds to ongoing security tensions in the region. Israeli forces have been dealing with periodic violence as the country navigates its complex security environment. Central Israel, which includes major population centers, has seen sporadic attacks over recent years.

Israeli authorities have not released details about the attacker or the specific circumstances of the shooting. Medical teams treated the wounded at the scene before transporting them to nearby hospitals. The incident prompted an immediate security response from Israeli forces in the area.

The shooting comes amid broader regional instability. Israel continues to manage security challenges on multiple fronts, including threats from militant groups in Gaza and the West Bank. Such attacks typically trigger heightened security measures and increased patrols in affected areas as authorities work to prevent follow-up incidents.

cards.headline: Flesh-eating screwworm found in second Texas case
cards.teaser: The U.S. confirmed a second case of screwworm in Texas, prompting Canada to restrict livestock imports from the country.
cards.body:
A second case of screwworm has been confirmed in Texas, prompting the state to declare a disaster emergency. The parasite, which had been eradicated from the United States since 1966, lays eggs in open wounds where larvae consume living flesh. The discovery triggered Canada to ban cattle imports from Texas.

U.S. officials are launching a multi-pronged response to combat the outbreak, including the use of flies and dogs as part of their eradication strategy. The screwworm poses a significant threat to livestock and other animals, with potential for severe damage and death if left untreated.

cards.headline: Peru holds presidential runoff between left and right candidates
cards.teaser: Peruvians vote in a tight presidential election between a leftist candidate and Keiko Fujimori, who would be the country's first female president.
cards.body:
Peru held a presidential runoff election between Keiko Fujimori, a right-wing candidate and daughter of former president Alberto Fujimori, and Roberto Sánchez, a leftist congressman and former trade and tourism minister. Fujimori had won 17% in the first round, while Sánchez secured 12%, edging out ultra-conservative Rafael López Aliaga.

The election reflected deep political polarization in a country struggling with instability. Peru had cycled through nine presidents in a decade, while rising crime and corruption scandals fueled voter concerns about governance and public safety. Voters faced a stark ideological choice between Fujimori's right-wing platform and Sánchez's leftist vision as they sought stability and solutions to the country's mounting challenges.

cards.headline: US Defense Secretary Hegseth draws criticism during D-Day speech in France
cards.teaser: Pete Hegseth compared European migration to an invasion during remarks in Normandy, prompting local residents to say he was not welcome.
cards.body:
US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth delivered remarks in Normandy on the 82nd anniversary of D-Day, drawing criticism for his characterization of European migration. Speaking at the site where allied forces launched their 1944 operation to liberate Nazi-occupied northwestern Europe, Hegseth compared contemporary migration to dangerous ideologies threatening the continent. He also criticized European defense spending during his remarks.

Residents of a nearby French village objected to the visit. The speech's tone and framing of migration policy prompted sharp reactions, with some viewing it as inappropriate for a ceremony honoring allied sacrifice in World War II.

cards.headline: Ukrainian drones strike St. Petersburg during Russian economic forum
cards.teaser: Drone attacks targeted St. Petersburg as Russia hosted its flagship economic event attended by President Vladimir Putin.
cards.body:
Ukrainian drones attacked St. Petersburg while Russia's major economic forum was underway in the city. The strikes disrupted what President Putin considers a flagship event for showcasing Russian economic policy and attracting foreign investment. Putin was attending the forum at the time of the attacks.

The timing of the strikes during the high-profile international gathering appeared designed to undermine the event's purpose and demonstrate Ukraine's capacity to reach deep inside Russian territory. St. Petersburg, Russia's second-largest city, lies hundreds of miles from the Ukrainian border.

cards.headline: Pope draws over one million to outdoor Mass in Madrid
cards.teaser: Pope Leo celebrated Mass before huge crowds in Madrid during a visit to Spain marked by a traditional flower-carpeted procession.
cards.body:
More than a million people gathered near Madrid's Plaza de Cibeles for an outdoor Mass celebrated by Pope Leo. Crowds pressed against barriers, waving flags and shouting "Long live the pope" as the pontiff arrived in his white popemobile. Some attendees tossed flower petals during his arrival at the central plaza.

The event marked the Pope's first visit to an EU country outside Italy and was likely the largest gathering of his week-long visit to Spain. The Pope urged world leaders to stop dividing electorates and to respect every human being. The Mass came during Spain's first papal visit in 15 years.

cards.headline: Health workers say U.S. foreign aid changes affected AIDS programs in Africa
cards.teaser: Providers in South Africa and Mozambique report that cancellation or redirection of PEPFAR funding has endangered vulnerable people.
cards.body:
Health care workers in South Africa and Mozambique report that shifts in U.S. foreign aid policy under the Trump administration have disrupted AIDS relief efforts. The changes involved cancellation or redirection of PEPFAR funding, the President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief that has long supported HIV treatment and prevention across Africa.

Providers working directly with patients say these funding changes have endangered vulnerable populations and resulted in loss of life. The disruptions have compromised their ability to continue serving those dependent on these programs.

cards.headline: Defense Secretary Hegseth criticizes European migration policy in D-Day speech
cards.teaser: Speaking in Normandy on the 82nd anniversary of the allied operation, Hegseth attacked Europe over migration.
cards.body:
U.S. Defense Secretary Hegseth delivered remarks in Normandy on the 82nd anniversary of D-Day, the Allied operation that liberated Nazi-occupied northwestern Europe. He used the occasion to criticize European migration policies, characterizing migration as a "beach invasion."

The speech drew attention for linking the historic military anniversary to contemporary migration debates in Europe.

cards.headline: U.S. men's soccer team completes final preparation before World Cup
cards.teaser: The national team played Senegal and Germany in their last matches before the tournament begins.
cards.body:
The U.S. men's national team selected two highly ranked opponents for their final World Cup preparations: Senegal and Germany. These competitive matchups provided a rigorous test against top-tier international competition as the team readied itself for the tournament.

The tune-up games demonstrated that the U.S. is prepared for the World Cup, which the country is co-hosting.

cards.headline: One million attend papal procession in Madrid
cards.teaser: Pope Leo arrived for Mass at a central plaza as crowds filled the streets for the first papal visit to Spain in 15 years.
cards.body:
More than one million people gathered in Madrid's streets near Plaza de Cibeles for an outdoor Mass led by Pope Leo. The crowd waved flags and shouted "Long live the pope!" as the pontiff arrived in his white popemobile, with some attendees tossing flower petals.

This marks the pope's first visit to Spain in 15 years and his first trip to an EU country outside Italy. During the event, he urged world leaders to stop dividing electorates and to respect every human being.

cards.headline: British Foreign Secretary confronts Vance over migrant remarks
cards.teaser: David Lammy told JD Vance his comments blaming Henry Nowak's death on migration were wrong.
cards.body:
British Foreign Secretary David Lammy said he told U.S. Vice President JD Vance that his comments about Henry Nowak's death were wrong. Vance had blamed Nowak's death on what he called the mass invasion of migrants.

Lammy stated that Nowak's death has nothing to do with mass migration. The exchange highlights tensions between the two governments over migration rhetoric and policy.

cards.headline: CaaStle CEO Stayed in Charge After Fraud Confession
cards.teaser: The board of fashion tech startup CaaStle allowed its chief executive to remain in her role after she confessed to defrauding the company.
cards.body:
Christine Hunsicker, CEO of fashion tech startup CaaStle, confessed to defrauding her own company but was permitted by the board to stay in charge. The company's final months included fake audits, stock buybacks, and a damage control strategy led by Hunsicker herself.

The board's decision to retain Hunsicker despite her admission raises questions about corporate governance and accountability at the startup. CaaStle operated in the fashion technology sector before its collapse.

cards.headline: China's Central Bank Extends Gold Buying Streak to 19 Months
cards.teaser: The People's Bank of China added gold to its reserves again, marking the 19th consecutive month of purchases as the country's foreign exchange reserves reached their highest level since 2015.
cards.body:
China's central bank continued its gold purchasing program, extending its buying streak to 19 months. The purchases come as the country's foreign exchange reserves climbed in May to levels not seen in nearly a decade.

The sustained gold acquisitions reflect China's ongoing strategy to diversify its reserve holdings. The buildup occurs while global gold prices face pressure from other market forces.

cards.headline: Paramount Considers Selling Kids Channels Amid Warner Bros. Merger Review
cards.teaser: Paramount is open to selling its children's television channels as regulators in Europe review its proposed merger with Warner Bros. Discovery.
cards.body:
Paramount has signaled a willingness to divest its kids channels to address European Union regulatory concerns over its proposed merger with Warner Bros. Discovery. The $110 billion deal is facing scrutiny from regulators on both sides of the Atlantic.

Industry workers gathered at a town hall to voice opposition to the merger, with some characterizing it as damaging to the American entertainment industry. A Paramount lawyer defended the deal during the meeting, asserting that certain opponents hold antisemitic views.

cards.headline: Bank of America Adjusts Broadcom Price Target After Earnings
cards.teaser: Bank of America reset its price target for Broadcom stock following the chip manufacturer's recent earnings report.
cards.body:
Bank of America revised its price target for Broadcom after the semiconductor company reported earnings. The announcement came as Broadcom's stock declined despite strong jobs data, triggering a broader sell-off in artificial intelligence related stocks.

Analysts have debated whether Broadcom's premium valuation is justified and whether the stock decline represents an overreaction to conservative guidance from the company. The earnings report and subsequent market reaction have drawn attention to investor expectations for companies in the AI chip sector.

cards.headline: Executives Deploy AI Twins to Handle Meetings and Messages
cards.teaser: Chief executives and professors are using artificial intelligence versions of themselves to answer questions and attend meetings as a productivity strategy.
cards.body:
A growing number of business leaders and academics have created AI replicas of themselves to manage routine communications and meeting attendance. The technology allows these digital twins to respond to inquiries and participate in discussions on behalf of their human counterparts.

Proponents describe the approach as a productivity enhancement that frees up time for higher priority work. The AI versions are designed to mimic the communication style and knowledge base of the individuals they represent.

cards.headline: WWE Shareholder Lawsuit Trial Canceled
cards.teaser: A trial for a shareholder lawsuit against WWE has been removed from the court schedule, sparing company leadership from an imminent court proceeding.
cards.body:
The trial for a lawsuit brought by WWE shareholders has been canceled and taken off the court calendar. The case had been scheduled to proceed but was removed from the docket.

The cancellation provides relief for WWE and its executives, including Vince McMahon, who would have faced testimony and examination during the trial. The lawsuit involved shareholders challenging corporate decisions at the professional wrestling company.

hero.headline: Bumblebees solve complex problems without training, study finds
hero.body:
Bumblebees can solve problems spontaneously despite their tiny brains, according to new research that demonstrates their remarkably advanced cognitive abilities. The study shows the insects performing a task previously documented only in large-brained animals like chimpanzees, elephants, and crows.

Researchers gave bumblebees an adapted version of a classic experiment from a century ago that first showed chimpanzees could retrieve an out-of-reach banana by stacking boxes. In the latest version, bees were tested on their ability to roll a polystyrene ball to a specific location and climb on top of it to access an artificial flower positioned on a low ceiling. The bees had never encountered this type of challenge before and received no training to perform it.

In the basic test, 75 percent of the bees successfully reached the flower. "This is essentially an insect version of the classic 'box-and-banana' problem," said Dr Olli Loukola, a behavioural ecologist at the University of Oulu, Finland, and senior author of the research. "What stands out about the result is that this kind of spontaneous problem solving is now demonstrated in an insect."

The findings challenge the long-held assumption that insects operate purely on instinct and mindless trial-and-error learning. To verify that the bees were genuinely solving the problem rather than simply enjoying rolling objects, scientists created increasingly complex versions of the challenge. In the final setup, bees explored two chambers before the test began, one containing the artificial flower. When scientists illuminated the chamber with red light to hide the blue flower from view and then introduced the ball, 23 out of 30 bees successfully positioned it beneath the flower's location based on memory alone.

"We are not claiming that bees think like humans," Loukola said. "But our findings show that miniature brains can generate flexible solutions to novel problems in ways we are only beginning to understand."

The research contributes to growing evidence that insect intelligence has been significantly underestimated. Previous studies have shown bees can count, recognize faces, and communicate through dance, but spontaneous tool use represents a notable leap in cognitive flexibility.

Prof Lars Chittka, a behavioural ecologist at Queen Mary University of London who was not involved in the research, emphasized the importance of these findings. "There's a general perception that intelligent behaviour requires big brains because we are big-brained and relatively intelligent among animals," Chittka said. "Bees are a model of how much intelligence you can squeeze into a small nervous system."

The study, published in the journal Science, raises fundamental questions about how intelligence evolved across different species and what minimal neural systems can achieve.

cards.headline: Oura Ring 5 compared to major wearable competitors
cards.teaser: Multiple reviews evaluate the newest Oura Ring against leading fitness trackers and smartwatches.
cards.body:
The Oura Ring 5 launched with comparisons to competing wearables including the Fitbit Air, Whoop MG, and Apple Watch. Reviews examined how the ring-based tracker stacks up against wrist-worn alternatives in health monitoring and daily use.

Multiple outlets tested the device over extended periods, with some calling it a new standard in wearable health tracking. The ring represents an advance in sensors that fit into a form factor smaller than traditional fitness watches. Comparisons focused on tracking accuracy, battery life, and whether the premium price justifies the upgrade over the previous Oura Ring 4 model.

cards.headline: School shooting survivor sues AI gun detection company after system failed
cards.teaser: A lawsuit challenges the reliability of artificial intelligence systems designed to identify weapons in schools.
cards.body:
A survivor of a school shooting filed a lawsuit against an AI gun detection firm after the company's system failed to spot a weapon. The case raises questions about the accuracy standards required for AI security technology deployed in educational settings.

The legal action focuses on whether the detection system performed as advertised and what level of reliability should be expected from automated threat identification tools. School districts across the country have adopted AI-based security systems as a response to campus violence, making the performance of these technologies a matter of public safety.

cards.headline: Ancient dragonflies had two-foot wingspans in oxygen-rich atmosphere
cards.teaser: The largest insects ever to exist grew to sizes impossible in modern atmospheric conditions.
cards.body:
The largest insects ever to exist were dragonflies with wingspans exceeding two feet. These giant insects thrived in Earth's ancient atmosphere, which contained significantly more oxygen than the air we breathe today.

The elevated oxygen levels of prehistoric Earth enabled insects to reach sizes that cannot survive in modern conditions. As atmospheric oxygen declined over time, the maximum size of insects decreased accordingly, reflecting the direct relationship between available oxygen and insect gigantism.

cards.headline: Soviet Luna 3 probe used onboard film development to photograph Moon's far side
cards.teaser: The 1959 mission employed innovative technology to transmit images from a hemisphere never before seen by humans.
cards.body:
In 1959, the Soviet Luna 3 probe captured 29 photographs of the Moon's far side, marking the first time humans had seen that hemisphere. The spacecraft developed the film onboard after taking the pictures, then scanned the negatives with a flying-spot beam to transmit the images back to Earth via radio.

The mission required solving the technical challenge of processing photographic film in space and converting the images into a format that could be transmitted across the distance between the Moon and Earth. The grainy photographs represented a significant achievement in both space exploration and remote imaging technology.

cards.headline: New telescope survey to catalog millions of unseen solar system objects
cards.teaser: A facility preparing to begin operations will search for objects in our solar system that have never been observed.
cards.body:
A new astronomical facility will begin a decade-long survey within months, aiming to discover millions of objects in the solar system that have never been seen. The project represents a comprehensive effort to catalog bodies orbiting in our cosmic neighborhood.

The survey will track objects ranging from small asteroids to distant bodies in the outer solar system. The facility's advanced capabilities will detect objects too faint or too distant for previous surveys, potentially revealing new classes of solar system bodies and improving understanding of how the planetary system formed and evolved.

cards.headline: Game director Hideo Kojima expresses skepticism about AI creating art
cards.teaser: The veteran developer said he does not expect to see artificial intelligence produce genuine art in his lifetime.
cards.body:
Hideo Kojima has expressed doubt that artificial intelligence will create genuine art during his lifetime. The legendary game director, best known for the Metal Gear series, stated he is not interested in pursuing AI-based creative work.

Kojima's skepticism aligns with broader concerns among creative professionals about whether AI systems truly generate original art or simply synthesize existing material. His stance contributes to an ongoing debate about AI's role in creative industries and whether current technology represents authentic artistic creation.

hero.headline: England defeat New Zealand in first Test at Lord's
hero.teaser: England completed victory over New Zealand in less than a session on day four.
hero.body:
England secured victory over New Zealand before lunch on the fourth day at Lord's, claiming the first Test of their three-match series.

New Zealand started day four needing 199 runs to win, having resumed on 55 for five. England's bowlers struck immediately, with Josh Tongue trapping Will Blundell lbw for four in the first full over of the morning. The quick dismissal set the tone for a dominant performance from the hosts.

Gus Atkinson was the standout bowler, taking five for 30 as England's seamers proved too strong for their visitors. The win came before lunch, demonstrating the extent of New Zealand's struggles on a pitch that continued to assist the fast bowlers throughout the Test.

The match had been dominated by seam bowling from the opening day. England's attack was spearheaded by Ollie Robinson, returning to the international stage after two years away from the set-up. Robinson made an immediate impact with a devastating performance on day one, taking four wickets including a remarkable three-wicket maiden over. His comeback impressed supporters and showed why England had been keen to get him back into the team.

The first day proved extraordinary, with 16 wickets falling in 60 overs of rain-affected play. Robinson bowled from the Nursery End and proved nearly impossible to face, with the pitch offering considerable assistance to all the quick bowlers. New Zealand's Kyle Jamieson and Will O'Rourke also took wickets, but it was the relentless quality of England's bowling attack that proved decisive.

When batting became possible, the most aggressive innings came from England's Harry Brook, who scored 56 from 71 balls. For New Zealand, Glenn Phillips' unbeaten 31 from 34 balls showed some resistance, as he attempted to counter-attack when his side found themselves in difficulty.

The pitch at Lord's remained treacherous throughout the Test, with short-pitched deliveries proving difficult to negotiate. Several batsmen were beaten or forced to defend desperately as the ball moved and lifted unpredictably.

England's victory marks the beginning of their rebuild following the Ashes series. The comprehensive nature of the win, achieved inside four days with New Zealand unable to mount a sustained challenge, will provide confidence heading into the remaining two Tests of the series.

The performance showcased England's strength in seam bowling and their ability to exploit helpful conditions. With Robinson back in the fold and bowlers like Atkinson delivering match-winning performances, England's attack appears well-equipped for the challenges ahead in their Test campaign.

cards.headline: Golden Knights rally from 4-0 deficit to beat Hurricanes in double overtime
cards.teaser: The Vegas Golden Knights recovered from a four-goal deficit to defeat the Carolina Hurricanes 5-4 in double overtime in Game 3 of the Stanley Cup Final on Satur.
cards.body:
The Vegas Golden Knights mounted an impressive comeback to defeat the Carolina Hurricanes 5-4 in double overtime during Game 3 of the Stanley Cup Final. Defenseman Shea Theodore scored the overtime winner, giving Vegas a 2-1 series lead.

Carolina dominated early, building a 4-0 advantage before Vegas tied the game with four consecutive goals. The dramatic rally forced the contest into overtime, where Theodore delivered the decisive goal.

cards.headline: Germany defeats United States in World Cup warm-up match
cards.teaser: Germany beat the USA 2-1 in a friendly ahead of the World Cup, but injuries overshadowed the result.
cards.body:
Germany defeated the United States 2-1 in a pre-World Cup friendly match. The game served as a final test for both teams before the tournament begins.

Injuries cast a shadow over the match despite the result. The USA showed the fight that coach Mauricio Pochettino wanted from his squad, but the loss provided a reality check heading into the World Cup. Both teams will assess their rosters as they prepare for group stage play.

cards.headline: Mitch Marner sets Stanley Cup Final hat trick record
cards.teaser: Vegas star Mitch Marner recorded the fastest hat trick in Stanley Cup Final history.
cards.body:
Mitch Marner made Stanley Cup Final history by recording the fastest hat trick ever in the championship series. The Vegas Golden Knights star's three goals came during Game 3 against the Carolina Hurricanes on Saturday night.

The Golden Knights mounted an impressive comeback from a four-goal deficit, ultimately winning 5-4 in double overtime. Shea Theodore scored the game-winner at 5:38 of the second overtime, giving Vegas a 2-1 series lead over Carolina.

cards.headline: Chase Elliott to start on pole at Michigan International Speedway
cards.teaser: Chase Elliott won the pole position and will lead Hendrick Motorsports at the NASCAR Cup race.
cards.body:
Chase Elliott secured the pole position for the NASCAR Cup race at Michigan International Speedway. He will lead Hendrick Motorsports to the green flag when the race begins.

The qualifying results set up a strong showing for Hendrick Motorsports at the track. Toyota has dominated at Michigan in recent races, but Chevrolet and Ford teams will look to challenge that streak with Elliott starting from the top spot.

cards.headline: Lionel Messi rested as Argentina faces Honduras in friendly
cards.teaser: Argentina rested Lionel Messi in a warm-up match against Honduras ahead of the World Cup.
cards.body:
Argentina chose to rest Lionel Messi in a pre-World Cup friendly against Honduras. The decision comes as teams manage player fitness before the tournament begins.

Brazil, Germany, Belgium and Portugal each won their warm-up matches ahead of the World Cup. Rafael Leao was sent off during Portugal's friendly. Teams are using these final matches to finalize tactics and assess player form before group stage competition starts.

cards.headline: Mystics coach Sydney Johnson ejected and escorted out by police
cards.teaser: Washington Mystics coach Sydney Johnson was ejected and escorted from the court by police after arguing with officials.
cards.body:
Mystics coach Sydney Johnson was ejected from Saturday's game against the Atlanta Dream after arguing with officials. He had to be held back during the confrontation and was subsequently escorted off the court by police.

The incident took place during a blowout loss for Washington on the road against the host Dream.

hero.headline: Former CBS News Anchor Scott Pelley Calls for Removal of Network News Chief Bari Weiss
hero.body:
Scott Pelley, a veteran journalist who spent decades at CBS News, was terminated by the network following a heated confrontation with management over recent staff cuts at 60 Minutes, according to reporting from the Guardian.

The conflict centered on changes made to the long-running news program last week, when CBS News fired its executive producer, executive editor, and two correspondents, Cecilia Vega and Sharyn Alfonsi, without providing specific reasons for the terminations.

During a Monday morning meeting with Nick Bilton, the newly appointed executive editor, Pelley criticized Bari Weiss, the former opinion commentator who joined CBS News in October as editor-in-chief. According to the Guardian, Pelley said Weiss was "murdering 60 Minutes" and accused her of not caring about the organization. "She was brought in to kill it and is doing exactly that," he told the group.

After the meeting, Weiss informed Pelley that his behavior was inappropriate. Pelley subsequently told staff members he expected to be terminated. On Tuesday evening, Bilton sent Pelley a message stating he had been "terminated for cause effective immediately." In the message, Bilton pointed to Pelley's conduct during their meeting, writing that Pelley had "hijacked" the conversation to "disparage me, my qualifications, and my intentions with remarkable incivility and contempt."

Bilton then notified the 60 Minutes staff of Pelley's departure in an email, stating the two had "parted ways." He noted his attempts to have conversations with Pelley over the weekend and that afternoon, though Pelley "was not" willing to find common ground.

Pelley's firing comes as the program faces significant upheaval. Earlier this year, journalist Anderson Cooper announced he was leaving the show. The departure leaves 60 Minutes with only three full-time correspondents ahead of its 59th season launch: Lesley Stahl, Bill Whitaker, and Jon Wertheim. Norah O'Donnell contributes to the program as well.

In response to his termination, Pelley issued a public statement accusing CBS News executives of silencing employees and instructing him to "inject falsehoods and bias" into his reporting. He emphasized that 60 Minutes has remained America's top program "because our beloved audience finds integrity, quality, and humanity in our stories."

Rome Hartman, a longtime 60 Minutes producer who retired last year, praised Pelley as "among the all-time greats of CBS News." He criticized Weiss and Bilton for firing Pelley for pushing back during a staff meeting, noting the irony given Weiss's company the Free Press positions itself against cancel culture.

Pelley joined CBS News in 1989 and served as anchor and managing editor of the CBS Evening News from 2011 to 2017 before joining 60 Minutes as a correspondent.

cards.headline: Ariana Grande Begins First Concert Tour in Six Years in Oakland
cards.teaser: The pop star performed the opening night of her Eternal Sunshine tour after a lengthy break from live performances.
cards.body:
Ariana Grande took the stage at Oakland Arena for the opening night of her Eternal Sunshine tour, marking her return to live performances after a six-and-a-half-year break from touring. The show represents her first tour since 2019.

Variety covered the performance and documented the complete setlist from the Sacramento concert. The tour draws its name from Grande's recent album and signals her reentry into regular touring following her extended hiatus from the concert circuit.

cards.headline: Bruce Springsteen Opens Music Center With Performance Featuring Jon Bon Jovi and Public Enemy
cards.teaser: The musician performed at the opening of a center dedicated to American music at Monmouth University.
cards.body:
Bruce Springsteen performed at the opening of the Bruce Springsteen Center for American Music, joined by Jon Bon Jovi and Public Enemy. The New York Times and Rolling Stone covered the concert, which took place as part of a series called Music America.

The center at Monmouth University is set to open on June 13. The opening concert featured multiple nights of performances, with the second night drawing the collaboration between Springsteen, Bon Jovi, and Public Enemy. The Asbury Park Press reported that the performance gave fans attending the Springsteen Center concert something to discuss.

cards.headline: Olivia Rodrigo Premieres Duet With The Cure's Robert Smith at Festival
cards.teaser: The pop singer revealed a collaboration with the rock legend during a surprise performance at Primavera Sound.
cards.body:
Olivia Rodrigo brought Robert Smith of The Cure onstage at the Primavera Sound festival to reveal a duet on her upcoming album. The song, titled What's Wrong With Me, had been kept secret until the festival performance. The album is scheduled for release within the next week.

The collaboration between Rodrigo and Smith represents a pairing of different musical generations. Rodrigo has established herself as a major pop artist, while Smith has led The Cure for decades. The reveal came as a surprise performance partway through Rodrigo's festival set.

cards.headline: Dua Lipa and Callum Turner Marry in Sicily Ceremony
cards.teaser: The singer and actor held a wedding celebration in Italy featuring a performance by Elton John.
cards.body:
Dua Lipa and Callum Turner married in a ceremony in Sicily. Elton John performed Your Song as part of the celebration, according to Vanity Fair. The couple also held nuptials in London, with The New York Times describing the event as featuring vintage glamour.

The Guardian reported that the wedding in Palermo drew mixed reactions from locals, with some questioning the attention given to the event. Vogue covered Lipa's wedding attire, which included leather elements in her first Italy wedding look. Just Jared provided additional details about the Sicily ceremony.

cards.headline: Kennedy Center Loses Lawsuit Against Musician Who Canceled Over Trump Naming Dispute
cards.teaser: A judge dismissed the venue's case against Chuck Redd, who withdrew from a performance after the center was renamed.
cards.body:
A judge dismissed a lawsuit filed by the Kennedy Center against musician Chuck Redd, who canceled a performance following a dispute over the venue's renaming. The case centered on Redd's decision to withdraw from a Christmas Eve show after the center incorporated Trump into its name.

Multiple outlets reported the court's decision. WUSA9 and ABC News described the dismissal of the Trump Kennedy Center lawsuit. The Washington Post and The Guardian both covered the ruling in favor of Redd. The New York Times reported on the judge's decision to throw out the suit brought by the Kennedy Center.

cards.headline: Charlie Puth Cancels Orlando Concert Due to Illness
cards.teaser: The singer announced on social media that he was instructed to rest and could not perform his scheduled show.
cards.body:
Charlie Puth announced via Instagram Story that he must cancel his Saturday concert in Orlando, Florida due to illness. The singer expressed his devastation over the decision, stating he is heartbroken to pull out of the performance.

Puth had been sick for several days and followed medical advice to rest rather than risk further health complications. Multiple outlets including TMZ and Variety reported on the cancellation.

hero.headline: Trump delays Ukraine drone deal despite Zelensky requests
hero.teaser: The Trump administration has not signed a major drone agreement with Ukraine despite months of negotiations and direct appeals from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky.
hero.body:
The Trump administration has not yet finalized a major drone agreement with Ukraine, a delay that concerns military experts monitoring U.S. efforts to modernize its drone capabilities. Negotiations between the two countries have been underway since at least September, with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky repeatedly calling for Washington to complete the deal.

Zelensky outlined the issue during an appearance on CBS Face the Nation, explaining that Ukraine had already accommodated American testing preferences. "The US wanted to test all types of our drones. We agreed to the way they wanted to test, train with, and use our systems in the air, on land, and at sea. But we still don't have a bilateral drone deal," he said.

The Ukrainian president emphasized the potential benefits of cooperation, noting that American companies possess advanced artificial intelligence technologies that Ukraine lacks. "In turn, we have many things they don't have, due to our extensive experience on the battlefield. I think this cooperation can be huge," Zelensky stated, while acknowledging that the agreement requires Trump's approval to move forward.

Trump has been dismissive of Ukraine's drone expertise, claiming the United States does not need Ukrainian assistance in this area. However, this position contradicts developments in the Middle East, where multiple countries are actively pursuing deals to acquire Ukrainian defensive drones and training for their personnel. These nations have faced repeated Iranian attacks using the same Shahed drones that Russia deploys against Ukraine.

Zelensky noted that Ukraine has already secured drone agreements with countries in the Middle East and Europe. "Now we are preparing a big drone deal with the EU. I hope we will reach the same agreement with our American partners," he said.

The delay comes as Ukraine continues to demonstrate its drone capabilities in combat. On Sunday, Ukrainian forces struck multiple Russian energy infrastructure targets, including the Saratov oil refinery in southwestern Russia and the Lazarevo pumping station in the Kirov region northeast of Moscow, located more than 1,200 kilometers from Ukrainian-controlled territory. Ukrainian forces also attacked a fuel depot in the Rostov region.

Russia responded with its own drone strikes across Ukraine, targeting civilian areas and energy facilities. One person died in Chernihiv after a Russian drone hit a parking lot, while attacks on the city left 40,000 people without power. Russian drones also struck Dnipro and an oil refinery in the Rivne region.

Meanwhile, Zelensky announced that Ukraine had received a new Iris-T missile launcher from Germany and appealed to allies for additional air defense ammunition. He emphasized the need for more missiles to strengthen Ukraine's ability to counter Russian aerial attacks.

cards.headline: White House AI policy adviser to step down at end of month
cards.teaser: Sriram Krishnan, a senior policy adviser on artificial intelligence at the White House, confirmed Saturday that he will leave his position at the end of this mo.
cards.body:
Sriram Krishnan, a senior White House policy adviser on artificial intelligence, confirmed Saturday that he will leave his position at the end of this month. The tech investor has been instrumental in shaping the Trump administration's approach to AI policy and strategy.

The White House has not announced a successor or explained how Krishnan's responsibilities will be reassigned. His departure occurs amid ongoing congressional debates over AI regulation, including proposals addressing safety standards, copyright protections, and workforce impacts.

cards.headline: Hemp industry pushes Congress to delay November ban on intoxicating products
cards.teaser: The intoxicating hemp industry is running out of time to convince Congress to delay or stop a ban on their products set to take effect in November.
cards.body:
A ban on hemp-derived intoxicating products is set to take effect in November unless Congress acts. Senator Mitch McConnell championed the prohibition, which was included in last fall's government funding legislation.

The hemp industry is lobbying lawmakers to intervene before the deadline. There is bipartisan interest in disrupting the ban, though no legislative solution has emerged yet. Industry advocates argue the ban will eliminate jobs and businesses that have grown around legal hemp products in recent years.

cards.headline: U.S. attorney in California opens election fraud investigation
cards.teaser: The Los Angeles U.S. attorney's office announced an investigation into election fraud in California's elections.
cards.body:
The Los Angeles U.S. attorney's office has launched an investigation into election fraud affecting California's elections. The announcement was made on Saturday.

The timing coincides with California's ongoing vote-counting process from its primary elections. Several races, including the Los Angeles mayoral primary, still have incomplete results as election officials continue processing ballots.

cards.headline: Trump to appear on Meet the Press as approval ratings hit new lows
cards.teaser: President Trump will sit for an interview on NBC's Meet the Press following a turbulent week marked by low approval ratings and public tensions with Senate Republicans.
cards.body:
President Trump is scheduled to appear on NBC's Meet the Press on Sunday following a week that saw his approval ratings reach new lows. The interview comes as tensions with Senate Republicans have spilled into public view ahead of midterm elections.

The president has faced mounting political pressure on key issues including the economy and other policy matters. The Sunday appearance offers Trump a platform to address growing concerns within his own party as midterm campaigns intensify.

cards.headline: Democrats see opportunity in Iowa Senate race after Turek primary win
cards.teaser: Democrats are viewing Iowa's U.S. Senate race with renewed optimism after state Rep. Josh Turek secured the party's nomination.
cards.body:
State Rep. Josh Turek won the Democratic nomination for Iowa's U.S. Senate seat on Tuesday, defeating state Sen. Zach Wahls in the primary. The 47-year-old two-time Paralympic gold medalist has built a track record of success in Republican-leaning districts.

Democrats view Turek's nomination as their strongest opportunity in years to compete for the seat. His ability to appeal beyond the party's traditional base in conservative areas gives strategists confidence heading into the general election.

cards.headline: Deb Haaland wins New Mexico Democratic primary for governor
cards.teaser: Former Biden administration official Deb Haaland won the Democratic primary for New Mexico governor and could become the first female Native American governor if elected.
cards.body:
Original Card Text (Unchanged)

Deb Haaland, a former Biden administration official, won the New Mexico Democratic primary for governor. If she prevails in the general election, Haaland would make history as the first female Native American governor in the United States.

Haaland previously served in the Biden administration before launching her gubernatorial campaign. She will face the Republican nominee in the November general election.

---

Reason: The source material provided is about Iran's World Cup team visa issues and other unrelated gubernatorial primaries in California and Iowa. It contains no information about Deb Haaland's New Mexico gubernatorial primary race, so the original card text is returned unchanged.
